sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Burnley host Brighton & Hove Albion at Turf Moor with the hosts 19th (20 points) and the visitors 11th (43). Burnley are winless in 6, while Brighton have 4 wins in 5 and have avoided defeat in the last 3 head-to-heads. The visitors arrive as favourites on form.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Burnley have 2 draws and 3 losses from their last 5, often ceding territory (around 40% possession) and allowing high shot volumes. Brighton have beaten Liverpool, Brentford and Nottingham Forest in that run, with only a narrow loss to Arsenal; Danny Welbeck has 4 goals in his last 5.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Last 2 meetings: Brighton 2-0 at home (January), 1-1 at Turf Moor (April 2024). Recent matchups have often been tight, with a trend towards fewer goals, and the home side frequently scoring first.

sections.subtitle: Season stats snapshot
sections.text: Burnley: 33 scored (16th), 61 conceded (20th); 41% average possession (20th); opponents’ big chances faced are league-high; 3.58 corners per game (18th). Brighton: 41 scored, 37 conceded; they carry a late scoring threat with a strong 76–90 minute output.

sections.subtitle: Key players and tactical notes
sections.text: Burnley’s threats include Zian Flemming (8 goals), Jaidon Anthony (7) and set-piece delivery from James Ward-Prowse. For Brighton, Pascal Gross has hurt Burnley before (3 assists across recent meetings), with Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh offering dribbling threat and Jan Paul van Hecke a set-piece outlet.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Thomas Bramall averages 3.4 yellows and 0.13 reds per game. Burnley average 1.68 yellows. Expect a moderate card count and a corner tally close to average, with recent head-to-heads slightly lower on corners.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Model probabilities point to Brighton (home 20%, draw 24%, away 56%) with 49% for both teams to score. Brighton should edge a close game; both teams to score is nearly balanced but leans towards ‘no’ given Brighton’s recent defensive record and Burnley’s limited creation.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Brighton & Hove Albion lead 1-0 at half-time at Turf Moor after Mats Wieffer scored on 43'. Brighton have controlled the ball (61% possession) and produced 3 shots on target to Burnley’s 2. Expected goals favoured Brighton (0.62) over Burnley (0.43). However, Burnley created the clearer openings, recording 2 big chances and 4 corners, but they missed both big chances. Pascal Gross supplied the assist for the opener.

halftimeSections.subtitle: First-half overview
halftimeSections.text: Brighton progressed higher up the pitch more consistently (final-third entries 30, penalty-area entries 16) and edged the duels (51%). Burnley carried threat from set-plays and early deliveries, helped by winning 60% of aerial duels and James Ward-Prowse’s supply (3 key passes, 2 big chances created). The hosts’ issue was efficiency in the box, with 2 big chances missed keeping them behind.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Brighton started on the front foot with a sustained spell. Burnley then responded with their strongest attacking phase around the middle of the half. After that, Brighton reasserted control with a long period of pressure up to the interval, with only a brief Burnley response before Brighton struck just before half-time.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key player notes
halftimeSections.text: Burnley: James Ward-Prowse has been the main creator (3 key passes, 2 big chances created). Jaidon Anthony found good positions but missed a big chance. At the back, Maxime Estève and Hjalmar Ekdal have dealt with crosses reasonably well. Brighton: Danny Welbeck has been the main outlet (2 shots on target, strong expected goals share). Mats Wieffer has contributed on both sides of the ball and took his chance well. Pascal Gross has linked play effectively and delivered the assist. Jan Paul van Hecke has read danger well in defence.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical outlook for second half
halftimeSections.text: Burnley should increase tempo and territory, using earlier crosses and set-piece delivery to exploit their aerial edge. Expect more runs beyond the last line to convert Ward-Prowse’s service into shots from closer range. Brighton are likely to manage the game with possession and selective transitions, aiming to isolate Welbeck against the centre-backs and use runners to attack second balls. If Burnley push full-backs higher, Brighton can target space behind on the counter.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Set-pieces, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: Corners at half-time: Burnley 4, Brighton 0. Yellow cards: Burnley 1, Brighton 0. With Burnley chasing, further corners for the hosts are likely and Brighton may add a few on transitions. Expect a slight rise in fouls as intensity increases; anticipate 2-3 second-half yellow cards combined. No red cards so far.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Next goal: Brighton. Rationale: their control of possession, territory and penalty-area entries points to another high-quality look, while Burnley’s finishing has been wasteful. Most likely scorer: Danny Welbeck given his first-half shot profile and positioning. Predicted full-time: Burnley 0-2 Brighton, with a single goal after the break.
